Ecoli levels on the rise on Cape Towns beaches

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Are the pristine waters of Clifton that clean?

Summary:
Heading for Cape Town to bask on the beaches this summer, escaping the drought and empty tourist spots? Well, be careful where you put your foot in the water. From Woodstock to Hout Bay, which includes the iconic beaches of Clifton and Camps Bay, there are no sewerage plants, untreated sewage empties out into Table Bay a few 100 meters off shore. If there is a strong onshore wind then that sewage is blowing back inland.
Aerial photographs taken two months ago in Camps Bay and Hout Bay clearly show the effluent stream. It’s a sobering thought considering there are several hospitals pumping pharmaceuticals along this stretch as well as an ever-increasing population. Now they are going to build a shopping mall in Clifton which will escalate the problem.



Further information:
Dr Jo Barnes has been challenging the City of Cape Town to address the e-coli and sewage drainage into Table Bay for years. She says the deep sea levels range between 16-20% over the safe e-coli limit which means the levels in the sea sand will be even higher. Despite providing this information to the City she says their responses are getting worse, they refuse to respond to any emails or requests for information. Dr Barnes will test the e-coli levels on Camps Bay beach for Carte Blanche and will have the results in two days.

Dr Leslie Petrik says the chemical compounds going out in the effluent pose a far greater danger. There are 87 000 different compounds in domestic and pharmaceutical waste which are know endocrine disruptions and they are not being treated in waste water treatment plants and definitely in untreated marine outfall pipes.

Script:


Links: “Is there anything that takes you closer to nature than getting into a Kayak and paddling out to season a beautiful day like this you have this spectacular view of Table Mountain and Lions Head in the background. The only trouble is right now is that we are paddling through smelly toxic sludge of human waste.
Script: 55 million litres of untreated effluent pumps into Table Bay every day. From Woodstock including the entire City Bowl, around to Hout Bay there are no waste water treatment works. Marine Conservation Photographer Jean Tresfon was horrified by what he was seeing and posted pictures on his blog site
Jean Tresfon “People just plainly didn’t believe that the City of Cape Town would pump untreated sewage into our sea. I had the idea to do the standard tourist shot of the City of Cape Town with the mountain in the back ground and signal hill and this time I put the plume in the foreground so that I had context and scale
Script: It went viral on social media putting the City of Cape Town under major pressure
Jean “Councillor Ernest Sonnenberg said well it’s not sewage because there aren’t any seagulls. There initial suggestion was its actually from a passing ship”
Script: We went out with Tracy Fincham to the outfall pipe which is 1.7 km out in the bay to see for ourselves. She has been taking guided kayaking trips for the past 17 years and says it’s definitely getting worse.
Tracy “Normally we see the birds and we just say let’s get the hell out of here, I didn’t realise it was such a big area”
Script: Earlier this year regular kayaker Eddie Bisset was violently ill for 3 days
Eddie Bissett: Well an Eskimo roll is when you go under the water it’s a self- rescue technique and I did one here in the bay, and that night I felt a bit weird the next day I had diarrhoea and gastro headache slight fever
Script: His doctor suggested he take water samples
Eddie Bissett 02 30 42 So I bought an independent survey team in and the e-coli levels were higher than they should have been.
Script: Tracy also fell terribly ill hours after she took in a lot of water
Tracy "They took blood samples and the doctor was stumped. I started antibiotics that didn’t work
Eddie Bissett “The storm water system that you see behind you there those pipes when you get a heavy rain here we get all kinds of stuff floating into the bay. Dead cats and tampons and condoms and nappies I mean it weird, it’s really gross “
Tracy “On certain days the water is brown, the stench is literally you can’t breath, it’s makes this really like cappuccino brown disgusting slosh slime on the surface of the water
Eddie Bissett: The problem is the onshore wind, it will blow that plume directly onto the beaches and onto the rocks you now and that’s where we recreate, that is the real problem
Script: Greg Oelofse Manager of Environmental Corporate Governance for the City of Cape Town disagrees
Greg “Three Anchor Bay the water quality and the smell and the associated stuff is a number of factors but it is not related to the outfalls or the plumes. Those are not going to transverse through that ocean in that high energy environment and then land up in that pocket bay. What has been tried on that particular storm water outlet is a chlorination system to try and improve that water quality there
Script: But kayakers and surfers are seeing it right along this stretch, not just in this inlet. After we left that morning Tracy took these pictures, the storm water spued out the foulest smelling effluent. When we return a few hours later these children were swimming in this water - oblivious. There are no warning signs despite the City’s acknowledging that the storm water is a problem
Eddie Bissett “One of them is at Camps Bay one of our busiest Blue Flag beaches and it’s going to be packed over Christmas.
Script: It was Jean Tresfon image of the plume off Camps Bay that raised the rate payers concern, they asked epidemiologist Dr Jo Barnes to conduct independent tests.
Jo Barnes “What we are looking at the moment is to find out whether the water that is sub surface on the beach is also contaminated. That would mean it is not only the ocean that is a risk to human health but the beach surface itself. I am specifically testing because it is a Blue Flag Beach and there is a marine sewer outfall pipe close by
Script: It’s a week later and the test results show 54 disease-causing enterococci bacteria in every 100 ml of water. That means a very high risk of children like these contracting an illness.

Jo Barnes “There is a big disconnect your exposure on a Sunday afternoon you and your kids and going home and getting ill on Tuesday morning. It’s a very underestimated connection, between your exposure and what you suffer from”
Greg Olifser “ I am not suggesting those tests are wrong there are also variations on a day to day basis so the source of e-coli on our coast is not a single source everything eventually lands up in the marine environment through a storm water system and there is plenty of e-coli contamination coming from there. There are seagulls on our beach, decaying kelp, people walking their dogs, and not cleaning them up so there are all kinds of sources of e-coli.
Jo Barnes “Internationally it is accepted that you do not release sewage into a bay. Because if the wind blows landward and it comes to the surface it takes the surface layer to the land and then it ducks under if the wind blows the other way it takes the surface layer away and then it comes back up to the land but there is a circle either this way or that way makes landfall.
Script: A large number of Cape Town’s beaches are in in bays with heavily polluted rivers flowing into them which in turn have storm water drains empting into them. The population has expanded so rapidly that many water ways are open untreated sewers.
Link: “This is the Disa river storm water runoff from a nearby settlement flows down this river and out into Hout Bay. The rest of the effluent produced by this entire area is pumped out to sea from a point no more than about 2 or 3 kms away. It’s what you might call a double wammy.
Jo Barnes “It’s been an old mantra amongst all the engineers that the solution to pollution lies in dilution, it has been thoroughly discredited over the last decade or so”
Link: Behind me is the Greenpoint pipe it pumps about 40 million litres of raw sewage into Table Bay each and every day. A mesh system catches anything more than 3 mm in diameter but everything else and I mean absolutely everything else is pumped out to sea.
Lesley Petrik “I am not as concerned about the microbes I am more concerned about the chemicals that are going out with the sewage”
Script: Chemist and Nano scientist Professor Leslie Petrik is working on how to eliminate chemical compounds from waste water treatment systems. These toxic chemicals are found in household cleaners, hair dyes, pharmaceutical products all known hormone or endocrine disrupters with serious health risks and they are all going straight out into the ocean.
John: Are the levels high enough to impact on human health?
Leslie “I don’t say these compounds are going to kill us straight away but you might develop cancer later in your life, your child might be born with a defect.
Script: In September she tested marine filter feeders near the Green Point outfall pipe and discovered that they eating our painkillers and drinking our coffee
Leslie “We found in our tests that the compounds were being up -concentrated in the marine organisms between 7 times and 70 times, they are accumulating in those organisms. So although you get this dispersion, those organisms like the filter feeders and the fish are constantly circulating that water through their body. And their bodies are absorbing those compounds out of the water.
John: “It’s not a once off impact like a running stomach or something like that it’s a long term impact?
Leslie “There is incontrovertible evidence by now that we are facing a public health crisis worldwide. Recently it’s been shown that citominofin which is an active ingredient in many painkillers is actually able to sterilise your male foetus in a certain period of your pregnancy and that will apply to humans as well as fish and they are starting to show that is the case. Now we are talking about collapsing fish populations because of over fishing but it is probably more to the point that these compounds are staying in the ocean and actually affecting the marine organism at a critical point
Script. Pharmaceutical waste from the many hospitals and clinics in the area are a major concern
Jo Barnes. Hospital sewage is not something you would like to expose the environment to, because there are lots of other antibiotics, x-ray contrast medium, all sorts of things in that has been totally untreated”
Leslie “We have seen its very difficult to break these compounds down even with advanced oxidation technologies because they simply break down into other compounds which then react with one another. So there is just no ways our current sewerage treatment plants or the marine outfall system is dealing with them.
Script: Councillor Sonnenberg Head of Utilities was unaware of the chemical threat. He says although pumping raw sewage into the ocean isn’t ideal, it’s done globally and that there is no land available in this area.
Councillor Sonnenberg “there is no solution at this point. What I am suggesting is that all of the approvals that we have to get to build such a facility there would be challenged at some point. So we are looking at it in the long term as I am sitting here I have 11 EIA’s in process for 11 waste water plants to be upgraded and that’s to unlock development in the rest of the City”
Script: The Integrated Coastal Management Act of 2009 states no one is allowed to discharge effluent into coastal water. In June the City discovered that its permits were outdated and in applying for the Coastal Waters Discharge Permit they engage in a public participation process. Prof Petrik and Dr Barnes made extensive submissions; neither got any response in the past 5 months.
Leslie “I have had no response from the city. But they are not even monitoring for these compounds, we have looked at the tests that they are doing on the water.
Script: There are 87000 different compounds which clearly can’t all be tested for but testing for indicator compounds would us an idea of the level of contamination. Kevin Samson head of Waste Water treatment says the public outcry has had an impact
Kevin Samson “We have asked the CSIR to broaden their scope to account for all the contaminants these scientists have raised. We will then take that information and make a decision on it”
Leslie Petrik “We are not talking about rocket science here, simple compounds like peroxide and a simple system like UV light is already a start in terms of breaking these compounds down.”
Jean “I understand there is a piece of land there that’s been going out to tender for development there and its right at the place where they need to build a sewage plant. Instead of building more hotels and shops perhaps we can build a sewage plant and actually clean up our sea”

There are 87 000 different compounds in domestic and pharmaceutical waste which are know endocrine disruptions and they are not being treated in waste water treatment plants and definitely in untreated marine outfall pipes.
